claim: Monte Buciero in Santoña hosts three principal fortifications: Fuerte de San Carlos (first line guarding the bay entrance, with 17th-c. origins from Juan de Maeda's 1688 reconstruction proposal), Fuerte de San Martín (second line on the Buciero slope, V-shaped with two superimposed levels), and Fuerte del Mazo / Fuerte de Napoleón (protecting the north of town, with the only watch-turret of its era preserved in Cantabria).
quote: Fue la segunda barrera de fuego, en la falda del Buciero. Construido en forma de uve, con dos pisos superpuestos. […] Llamado anteriormente fuerte de Mazo. Se encuentra protegiendo la parte norte de la población […] Se conserva la garita de vigilancia, única de esta época en Cantabria.

claim: Playa de la Salvé in Laredo is shell-shaped, measures 4,250 m in length, and sits within a wide bay sheltered by Monte Buciero (Santoña).
quote: La playa tiene forma de concha y una longitud de 4.250 metros […] se desarrolla dentro de una amplia bahía al abrigo de la protección del Monte Buciero (Santoña).

claim: The cabaña pasiega is a vernacular stone structure of the three Pas river valleys serving dual cattle-and-living use — ground floor as stable, first floor as hayloft (or as a 'vividora' residential cabin) — built on stone with wooden frames; some 10,000 such cottages were built mainly in the 18th–19th centuries across the scattered rural settlements of the Pasiegos valleys.
quote: simple building, constructed for cattle farming […] built on stones with rustic doors on wooden frames, small windows […] first floor used as a hayloft and the ground floor as stable […] 'vividora' cottage has additional comforts for residential, prolonged usage.
